decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm approach to the cup, lifting into a continuous elbow-up configuration; left arm remains home.
Move above and behind the cup, progressively pointing the open fingers downward for a rim grasp.
Align the downward right gripper over the cup's near-right rim, with clearance before descending.
Descend slowly to straddle the cup rim; retain open fingers until the next visual check.
Close on the cup rim and make a small test lift; retention must be checked visually.
Lift the retained cup clear of the table while starting the left arm toward the vase; keep the cup closed and upright.
Advance the left arm above the vase approach corridor with open fingers, keeping the held cup stationary.
Bring the left fingers toward a top rim grasp on the vase, with gradual downward orientation and no arm crossing.
Align the left gripper above the vase's right rim, maintaining clearance and keeping the cup held still.
Set the left fingers just below the vase rim and close gently in place; the cup stays held by the right arm.
Test vase retention with a slow vertical lift, replanning from the observed pose after contact limited the descent.
The vase did not lift. Reopen and shift the left grasp toward the right rim so one finger can enter the opening and the other remain outside.
Narrow the left opening before advancing over the vase rim, avoiding the lip contact that blocked the previous descent.
The left inner finger is now over the vase opening. Lower slightly, pinch the rim, and begin a small retention test.
Test the adjusted vase grasp by lifting vertically with the left gripper closed; keep the ball-filled cup stationary.
The vase remained on the table. Shift the reopened left fingers inward toward the visible rim and lower to improve engagement.
Lower the left fingers a little further around the visible vase rim and close in place, maintaining the right cup grasp.
Test whether the newly closed left grasp retains the vase during a small upward motion before attempting any transfer.
The vase still did not lift. Reposition the left grasp toward the near-right lip, away from the far wall, with fingers reopened.
Clear the outer left finger past the right edge of the vase lip, then lower and pinch while the inner finger remains in the opening.
Check the latest rim pinch with a small lift and slight inward translation, looking for vase motion before transporting it.
The rim grasp did not retain the vase. Withdraw and rotate toward a horizontal neck grasp instead of repeating the top pinch.
Reorient the left gripper horizontally behind the vase neck, with wide jaws and clearance above the vase.
Lower the horizontal left gripper toward neck height, keeping open jaws outside the vase and the right cup steady.
Approach the vase neck horizontally with open left fingers, lowering in small increments and preserving elbow configuration.
Close the left gripper around the vase neck and make a short lift to check retention visually.
Raise the neck grasp a little farther and shift inward slightly to determine whether the vase follows.
The vase did not follow. Reopen and advance farther around the neck rather than pinching its front surface.
Withdraw the left arm from the vase. Since the vase has not moved, switch to a cup handover and pour using the left workspace.
Move the left arm toward the central cup handover area, rotating open fingers to approach the cup body from the left.
Continue the left approach toward the held cup, orienting for a body grasp while staying on the left side.
Advance the open left jaws around the cup body for handover; right grip stays closed throughout alignment.
Close the left gripper around the cup body while the right still supports its rim; inspect the dual grasp before release.
The left fingers appear short of the cup body. Reopen and advance a few centimeters while the right arm continues supporting the cup.
Separate the wrists and present the held cup from the right side for a safer body handover, keeping its opening upward.
Present the cup at a moderate tilt and align the left jaws with its body, keeping all balls below the lip and wrists separated.
Align the left jaws laterally with the cup body using the current wrist view, keeping the right support fixed.
Center the left fingers around the cup and close for handover, retaining right support until the grasp is visually checked.
Release the right rim grip and withdraw gently while keeping the left body grasp closed; verify that the cup stays with the left hand.
The cup appears retained by the left hand. Carry it leftward while restoring upright orientation; withdraw the empty right arm toward home.
The cup slipped during handover and balls are visible outside it. Stop the left transport and clear the right arm to assess the settled objects.
Approach the fallen cup from above with the left hand for recovery, while keeping the right arm clear of the scattered balls.
Align the left gripper for a downward grasp of the fallen cup; finish clearing the right arm toward its origin.
Move the open left fingers forward over the fallen cup, approaching slowly from above and avoiding the scattered balls.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller forward increments and a less vertical approach to preserve joint continuity.
Recover the nearest scattered ball with a small left-finger pinch, using the table image to align the fingertips rather than the wrist.
The ball is still just beyond the left fingertips. Advance a small amount with a narrow opening, pinch, and test retention.
Lift the closed left fingers and shift away from the scattered balls to check whether the pinch retained a ball.
The previous pinch was empty. Align the left fingers over the isolated leftmost ball and lower the fingertip pads to the ball's height.
Fine-align the visible ball between the left fingertip pads, close slowly, and perform a short retention lift.
The ball remains below the fingertip pads. Reopen narrowly and lower in small increments to reach its height before closing.
Advance the narrowly opened fingertips around the visible ball, close, and test a minimal lift while relieving table contact.
Change to a vertical pinch above the ball, lifting and opening first to avoid pushing it along the table.
Fine-align the vertical left pinch over the visible ball, correcting lateral and forward offset before closing.
Follow the displaced ball using its current head and wrist image positions, keeping the open pinch vertical and within the left workspace.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating for motion. Use smaller lateral increments and a slightly angled pinch while retreating the wrist from extension.
Center the nearest ball deeper between the fingertip pads, then close slowly without dragging across the table.
The ball is visibly between the left fingertips. Lift and retreat slightly with the grip closed to verify retention before carrying it to the vase.
The ball remains visibly retained. Lift it above vase-rim height while carrying it leftward, with the empty right arm stationary.
Carry the retained ball toward the vase opening at a safe height, maintaining the closed left pinch.
Replan after the continuity rejection: retract the wrist slightly and angle the retained ball toward the vase opening without extending the elbow further.
